reproduction_target: Reproduce the BasCoD background-selection results/figures from the manuscript: apply the BasCoD spectral subspace-inclusion test (R, BasCoD.R) to evaluate and select appropriate background datasets for contrastive dimension reduction across single-cell datasets (mouse protein data used with cPCA; Norman et al. Perturb-seq; mouse intestinal data via ContrastiveVI; HCA bone-marrow erythroid post-trajectory analysis via Lamian/Slingshot; Jerber et al. population-scale scRNA-seq with ROT treatment), corroborating previously published cPCA/ContrastiveVI analyses and demonstrating background calibration for a designed scRNA-seq experiment. The repo ships 4 tutorial notebooks that 'reproduce some of the results reported in the manuscript'.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-computational-stage from Methods prose plus repo README/tree (stage-1 prose only; BasCoD.R and 4 .ipynb tutorials NOT read line-by-line). Methods are primarily mathematical (latent-variable models, spectral subspace-inclusion test); named external tools are cPCA, ContrastiveVAE/ContrastiveVI, and Slingshot/Lamian (trajectory). No wet-lab reproduced: the designed scRNA-seq dataset is reused input, not regenerated (W=0).

steps.label: Data acquisition of the single-cell datasets: mouse protein data (from cPCA GitHub repo, Data_Cortex_Nuclear.csv), Norman et al. Perturb-seq and mouse intestinal data (via ContrastiveVI tutorial), HCA bone-marrow (Lamian slingshot_data.rda), Jerber et al. population-scale scRNA-seq (Zenodo), plus figshare/Google-Drive-hosted tutorial datasets

Contrastive dimension reduction to obtain target/background low-dimensional embeddings: cPCA (Contrastive PCA) / CVLM for linear cases and ContrastiveVAE/ContrastiveVI for the VAE/variational-inference cases, following the referenced methods' tutorials

Trajectory / post-trajectory analysis for the HCA bone-marrow erythroid-differentiation case (Slingshot / Lamian), producing the embeddings on which BasCoD post-trajectory background selection operates

BasCoD testing framework (R; code/functions/BasCoD.R): spectral subspace-inclusion goodness-of-fit test to identify valid background datasets (B) and reproduce manuscript figures via the 4 tutorial notebooks; requires R (>=4.2.2) and MASS

headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on all 4 computational steps. R★ not assignable at stage1. gaps.how_to_close: Ship an renv.lock (or conda-lock/pixi.lock) capturing R version, MASS and all transitive package versions, plus the exact versions of cPCA/ContrastiveVI/Slingshot used, for a declared platform; or provide a container digest.

gaps.missing: Datasets are sourced heterogeneously via third-party links rather than primary versioned accessions: mouse protein data from the cPCA GitHub repo (blob), Perturb-seq/mouse-intestinal from the ContrastiveVI tutorial, HCA-BM from Lamian's slingshot_data.rda (GitHub blob), and tutorial data from a Google Drive folder (mutable) and a figshare file. Only the Jerber et al. dataset is on Zenodo (versioned). No GEO/SRA/ENA/dbGaP accession is given for the designed scRNA-seq experiment.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit or mirror all input matrices in a versioned archive (Zenodo/figshare with DOI) with a manifest mapping each dataset to the manuscript figures; replace the mutable Google Drive link with an immutable snapshot; cite primary accessions where they exist.

gaps.missing: Parameters for the external contrastive DR steps (cPCA contrast parameter alpha, latent dimensionality; ContrastiveVI latent dims / epochs / seeds) and for the BasCoD test itself (number of retained embedding dimensions, test thresholds/significance levels, random seeds) are not specified in the Methods prose; they are deferred to external tutorials and the repo notebooks.
gaps.how_to_close: State all analysis parameters and random seeds in the Methods or a supplementary table, and pin them inside the tutorial notebooks.

gaps.missing: The repo has a LICENSE but no tagged release and no Zenodo/DOI archive; the paper links a floating HEAD rather than a specific commit or archived snapshot. Reproduction is pinned to whatever HEAD happens to be at read time.
gaps.how_to_close: Mint a tagged release archived to Zenodo (DOI) and cite the specific commit/DOI in the paper.
